result.title: Tight PAC-Bayes Generalisation Guarantees for Large Language Model Judges
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) judges are increasingly used to monitor the outputs of LLM-based AI agents, yet formal guarantees on the reliability of these judges remain largely absent, limiting confidence in their use for safety-critical oversight. We consider certifying such a judge and define its risk over safety classifications of prompt--response pairs drawn from a deployed generator. We apply a PAC-Bayes framework to this setting, refining existing compression-based methodology with the use of tighter bounds and more efficient coding. We show that standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning can yield non-vacuous and even tight certificates for safety judges, for both classification and Brier risk, without holding out data for validation. We introduce LoRA-GT, which shares a single quantisation scale across layers and achieves the tightest certificates with minimal degradation in predictive performance. Across five guardrail models and four benchmarks, we find that certificate tightness is governed more by adaptation complexity than by base model scale. Finally, we show how far quantisation can be pushed before the resulting increase in risk outweighs the bound tightening gained from shorter descriptions. Together, these results provide a practical route toward certifiable scalable oversight and offer insight into how the complexity of safety adaptations shapes generalisation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文为评估 LLM 智能体输出的安全判定器（LLM judge）建立 PAC-Bayes 泛化证书：改进基于压缩的界与编码效率，提出跨层共享量化尺度的 LoRA-GT，在五个 guardrail 模型、四个基准上得到非空泛甚至较紧的证书，并考察量化强度与风险上升之间的权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 主体是安全分类器的可靠性认证，与 latent 推理状态无直接关系；但把「适配复杂度」而非基座规模与泛化风险挂钩的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 LoRA/视觉旁路等训练监督的泛化代价与容量取舍。
